## Tag-name Constants and Categories

String-literal unions identifying tag groups per the HTML5 spec.

### TagName

```ts
type TagName =
  | AnchorTagName | TextLevelTagNames | EditsTagNames | EmbeddedTagNames
  | TabularTagNames | GroupingTagNames | SectioningTagNames
  | InteractiveTagNames | UntranslatableTagNames;
```

### AnchorTagName

```ts
type AnchorTagName = 'a';
```

### TextLevelTagNames

```ts
type TextLevelTagNames =
  | 'em' | 'strong' | 'strike' | 'small' | 'big' | 's' | 'cite' | 'q'
  | 'dfn' | 'abbr' | 'acronym' | 'ruby' | 'rt' | 'rp' | 'data' | 'time'
  | 'tt' | 'code' | 'var' | 'samp' | 'kbd' | 'sup' | 'sub'
  | 'i' | 'b' | 'u' | 'mark' | 'bdi' | 'bdo' | 'span' | 'br' | 'wbr';
```

### EditsTagNames

```ts
type EditsTagNames = 'ins' | 'del';
```

### EmbeddedTagNames

```ts
type EmbeddedTagNames =
  'audio' | 'canvas' | 'embed' | 'iframe' | 'img' | 'math'
  | 'object' | 'picture' | 'svg' | 'video';
```

### TabularTagNames

```ts
type TabularTagNames =
  'table' | 'tbody' | 'thead' | 'tfoot' | 'tr' | 'td' | 'th';
```

### GroupingTagNames

```ts
type GroupingTagNames =
  'p' | 'hr' | 'pre' | 'blockquote' | 'ol' | 'ul' | 'dir' | 'menu'
  | 'li' | 'dl' | 'dt' | 'dd' | 'figure' | 'figcaption'
  | 'main' | 'div' | 'xmp' | 'listing' | 'plaintext';
```

### SectioningTagNames

```ts
type SectioningTagNames =
  'body' | 'article' | 'section' | 'nav' | 'aside'
  | 'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3' | 'h4' | 'h5' | 'h6' | 'hgroup'
  | 'header' | 'footer' | 'address';
```

### InteractiveTagNames

```ts
type InteractiveTagNames =
  'form' | 'label' | 'input' | 'button' | 'select' | 'progress'
  | 'meter' | 'fieldset' | 'legend' | 'textarea' | 'output'
  | 'details' | 'summary' | 'dialog';
```

### AttribTagNames

```ts
type AttribTagNames =
  'accesskey' | 'datalist' | 'source' | 'track' | 'caption'
  | 'colgroup' | 'col' | 'option' | 'optgroup' | 'param';
```

### MetadataTagNames

```ts
type MetadataTagNames = 'head' | 'title' | 'base' | 'link' | 'meta';
```

### UnsupportedTagNames

```ts
type UnsupportedTagNames = 'area' | 'map';
```

### UntranslatableTagNames

```ts
type UntranslatableTagNames =
  AttribTagNames | UnsupportedTagNames | MetadataTagNames;
```

## Other Exports and Utilities

Functions, default values, and re-exported entries that don't fit the above buckets.

### TRenderEngine (re-export)

The TRE class. See "TRE Types" → "TRenderEngine (class)" above. The `index.mdx` page in `Other Exports` points to the same constructor.

### TChildrenRenderer (component re-export)

```ts
const TChildrenRenderer: FunctionComponent<TChildrenRendererProps>;
```

Renders a collection of TNodes; pair with `useTNodeChildrenProps`.

### isDomElement

```ts
function isDomElement(node: any): node is Element;
```

Type guard for `domhandler` `Element`.

### isDomText

```ts
function isDomText(node: any): node is Text;
```

Type guard for `domhandler` `Text`.

### domNodeToHTMLString

```ts
function domNodeToHTMLString(
  root: Node | null,
  reporter?: DomNodeToHtmlReporter,
  depth?: number,
): string;
```

Serialize a DOM tree back to its HTML string representation.

### DomNodeToHtmlReporter

```ts
interface DomNodeToHtmlReporter {
  (node: Node | null, depth: number, html: string): void;
}
```

Per-node callback invoked during HTML stringification.

### getNativePropsForTNode

```ts
function getNativePropsForTNode<T extends TPhrasing | TText | TBlock>(
  props: TDefaultRendererProps<T>,
): T extends TBlock ? ViewProps & { onPress?: () => void } : TextProps;
```

Extract the React Native props that would be passed to `Text` / `View` / `GenericPressable` by `TDefaultRenderer`. Use when wrapping a different native component (e.g. `Animated.Text`).

### collapseTopMarginForChild

```ts
function collapseTopMarginForChild(
  n: number,
  tchildren: readonly TNode[],
): number | null;
```

Compute the collapsed top margin for the n-th child. Returns `null` when no collapsing applies.

### splitBoxModelStyle

```ts
function splitBoxModelStyle(styles: NativeBlockStyles | NativeTextStyles): {
  boxModelStyle: /* margin/padding/border/positioning subset */;
  otherStyle:    /* remainder */;
};
```

Separate box-model styles from the rest — useful when wrapping a `Text` in a `View` to apply padding/borders that `Text` cannot.

### buildTREFromConfig

```ts
function buildTREFromConfig(props: TRenderEngineConfig): TRenderEngine;
```

Build a `TRenderEngine` from the same configuration object the `TRenderEngineProvider` accepts. Useful in tests and for debugging the TRE layer.

### setMarkersForTNode

Re-export of `SetMarkersForTNode` documented under TRE Types — the type alias for marker-mutator functions.

### markers

Re-export of the `Markers` interface documented under TRE Types.

### defaultHTMLElementModels

A typed map of every built-in `HTMLElementModel` keyed by tag name — full shape is `DefaultHTMLElementModelsStatic` documented above. Use `defaultHTMLElementModels.a.extend({...})` to derive a custom model.

### defaultSystemFonts

```ts
const defaultSystemFonts: string[];
```

A handful of platform-default font names — fork via `[...defaultSystemFonts, 'MyFont']` and pass into `RenderHTMLProps.systemFonts`. On Expo, prefer `Constants.systemFonts`.

### defaultListStyleSpecs

```ts
const defaultListStyleSpecs: Record<DefaultSupportedListStyleType, ListStyleSpec>;
```

Built-in counter-style renderers for `none`, `disc`, `circle`, `square`, `decimal`, the roman / alpha / greek series, and `disclosure-*`.

### useAmbientTRenderEngine

```ts
function useAmbientTRenderEngine(): TRenderEngine;
```

Access the `TRenderEngine` instance provided by the closest `TRenderEngineProvider`.

### useComputeMaxWidthForTag

```ts
function useComputeMaxWidthForTag(tagName: string): (cw: number) => number;
```

Resolve the max-width function configured via `computeEmbeddedMaxWidth` for a given tag.

### useContentWidth

```ts
function useContentWidth(): number;
```

Read the ambient `contentWidth` from context.

### useDocumentMetadata

```ts
function useDocumentMetadata(): DocumentMetadata;
```

Access parsed HTML metadata from the closest `RenderHTMLSource`.

### useNormalizedUrl

```ts
function useNormalizedUrl(initialUrl: string): string;
```

Normalize a relative or protocol-relative URL into an absolute one using the active `baseUrl` (from `<base>`, `source.baseUrl`, or `source.uri`). RFC 1808 semantics.

### useRendererProps

```ts
function useRendererProps<R extends RenderersProps = RenderersProps, K extends keyof R = keyof R>(
  tagName: K,
): R[K];
```

Read the deep-merged renderer props for a given tag (the `renderersProps[tagName]` from `RenderHTMLProps`).

### useSharedProps

```ts
function useSharedProps(): RenderHTMLAmbiantSharedProps;
```

Read the resolved `RenderHTMLSharedProps` (defaults filled in).

### useTNodeChildrenProps

```ts
function useTNodeChildrenProps(props: TNodeChildrenRendererProps): TChildrenRendererProps;
```

Translate `TNodeChildrenRenderer`-style props (with `tnode`) into `TChildrenRenderer` props (with `tchildren`) — useful when slicing a TNode's children into chunks (e.g. injecting ads between paragraphs).

### useIMGElementState / useIMGElementStateWithCache / useIMGElementProps

```ts
function useIMGElementState(props: UseIMGElementStateProps): IMGElementState;

function useIMGElementStateWithCache(
  props: UseIMGElementStateWithCacheProps,
): IMGElementStateError | IMGElementStateSuccess;

function useIMGElementProps(props: InternalRendererProps<TBlock>): IMGElementProps;
```

Build the image state machine in custom renderers or convert internal renderer props into props consumable by `IMGElement`.

### useInternalRenderer

```ts
function useInternalRenderer<T extends TagName>(
  tagName: T,
  props: InternalRendererProps<any>,
): T extends InternalSpecialRenderedTag
  ? InternalRendererConfig<ReturnType<typeof specialRenderersConfig[T]['hook']>>
  : InternalRendererConfig<TDefaultRendererProps<any>>;
```

Reuse internal renderer logic for custom renderers. `tagName` must be invariant.

## Externals

Re-exports of `domhandler` DOM types (the same shapes returned by `htmlparser2`/`parseDocument`). The component models above hold references to these.

### Node

`domhandler` base node. Fields:

```ts
type Node = /* abstract */;
// Common fields (inherited by Document/Element/Text/NodeWithChildren):
//   parent: ParentNode | null
//   prev:   ChildNode  | null
//   next:   ChildNode  | null
//   startIndex: number | null         // requires withStartIndices
//   endIndex:   number | null         // requires withEndIndices
//   sourceCodeLocation?: SourceCodeLocation | null  // parse5 only
//   type: ElementType
// Method:
//   cloneNode<T extends Node>(this: T, recursive?: boolean): T;
```

### NodeWithChildren

```ts
interface NodeWithChildren extends Node {
  children: ChildNode[];
}
```

Abstract base for any node that can contain children.

### Document

```ts
interface Document extends NodeWithChildren {
  type: ElementType.Root;
  'x-mode'?: 'no-quirks' | 'quirks' | 'limited-quirks';  // parse5 only
}
```

DOM root produced by `TRenderEngine.parseDocument(html)`.

### Element

```ts
interface Element extends NodeWithChildren {
  type: ElementType.Tag | ElementType.Script | ElementType.Style;
  name: string;                          // tag name (lowercase)
  attribs: Record<string, string>;
  // x-attribsNamespace?: ...            // parse5 only
  // x-attribsPrefix?: ...               // parse5 only
}
```

A DOM element node. The `domNode` referenced from `TNodeShape.domNode` is always an `Element`.

### Text

```ts
interface Text extends Node {
  type: ElementType.Text;
  data: string;
}
```

A text node. `TText.textNode` is a `Text`.

## Implementation notes

- `TNodeShape`, `TBlock`, `TPhrasing`, `TText`, `TDocument`, `TEmpty`, `TNodeDescriptor`, `TNodeType`, `TNodePrintOptions`, `Markers`, `SetMarkersForTNode`, `DocumentContext`, `NativeBlockStyles`, `NativeTextStyles`, `WebBlockStyles`, `WebTextStyles`, `ExtractTNodeFromType` are declared in `packages/transient-render-engine/lib/typescript/tree/tree-types.d.ts`.
- `HTMLElementModel`, `HTMLElementModelShape`, `HTMLContentModel`, `defaultHTMLElementModels`, `DefaultHTMLElementModelsStatic`, `ElementModelBase`, `NativeElementModel`, `CustomElementModel`, `ElementCategory`, `TagName` and all `*TagNames` aliases live in `packages/transient-render-engine/lib/typescript/model/*.d.ts`.
- All CSS prop-key aliases, `CSSProcessorConfig`, `MixedStyleDeclaration`, `CSSFlattenProcessedTypes`, `MixedSizeCSSPropertiesKeys`, `WebTextFlowProperties`, `WebBlockRetainProperties`, and native-style extras come from `packages/css-processor/lib/typescript/{config,property-types,native-types,processor-types,CSSProcessor}.d.ts`.
- `ReactNativeProps`, `ReactNativePropsDefinitions`, `ReactNativePropsSwitch`, `StylessReactNativeProps`, `StylessReactNativeTextProps`, `StylessReactNativeViewProps` live in `packages/transient-render-engine/lib/typescript/helper-types.d.ts`.
- Renderer prop interfaces (`TNodeRendererProps`, `RendererBaseProps`, `TDefaultRendererProps`, `InternalRendererProps`, `CustomRendererProps`, `TChildProps`, `TChildrenBaseProps`, `TChildrenRendererProps`, `TNodeChildrenRendererProps`, `PropsFromParent`, `RenderersProps`, `RenderHTMLSharedProps`, `RenderHTMLAmbiantSharedProps`, `RenderHTMLConfig`, `RenderHTMLSourceProps`, `RenderHTMLProps`, `HTMLSource*`, `DocumentMetadata`, `GenericPressableProps`, `ImageDimensions`, `*ListStyleSpec`, `DefaultSupportedListStyleType`, `UnitaryCounterRendererProps`, `EmbeddedHeadersProvider`, `FallbackFontsDefinitions`, `HTMLElementModelRecord`, `AElementConfig`, `ImgElementConfig`, `ListElementConfig`) live in `packages/render/lib/typescript/shared-types.d.ts`.
- Image-state and `IMGElement` prop types live in `packages/render/lib/typescript/elements/img-types.d.ts`.
- `Custom*Renderer`, `Internal*Renderer`, `CustomTagRendererRecord`, `InternalTextContentRenderer` live in `packages/render/lib/typescript/render/render-types.d.ts`.
- `useInternalRenderer`, `InternalSpecialRenderedTag`, `InternalRendererConfig` live in `packages/render/lib/typescript/hooks/useInternalRenderer.d.ts`.
- Helpers (`buildTREFromConfig`, `collapseTopMarginForChild`, `splitBoxModelStyle`, `domNodeToHTMLString`, `getNativePropsForTNode`, `DomNodeToHtmlReporter`) live in `packages/render/lib/typescript/helpers/*.d.ts`.
- Externals (`Document`, `Element`, `Node`, `NodeWithChildren`, `Text`) come from the `domhandler` package and are re-exported through `@native-html/transient-render-engine`.

# Contributing and Development

## Getting Help

### A User's Guide to Getting Help

### Decision table

Please read all the entries bellow before choosing the one that best fits your case, and proceed with the recommendations.

| Issue |
|---|
| I am encountering a failure |
| The library is not honoring an area of the CSS/HTML standard |
| The library is not behaving as it claims or should |
| I want to do X with this library, is it possible? |
| I am having trouble to understand how to use a specific feature |

### I am encountering a failure.

I am using `@native-html/render` and I am witnessing a failure such as:

- A Red screen of death during development that is caused by an object of this library;
- A failure while building the app for production;
- A crash or exception when rendering a component of this library.

**Recommendations**

1. Read the [FAQ](https://native-html.github.io/render/docs/faq).
2. Take a look at [native-html-render on StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/native-html-render) or [react-native-render-html on StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/react-native-render-html) for similar questions.
3. Take a look at [our issue tracker](https://github.com/native-html/render/issues) for similar questions.
4. If you still don't have a solution, you can choose one or more:
   - A. Submitting a Bug Report (see Contributing > Opening Tickets).
   - B. Going to [our Discord #support channel](https://discord.gg/dbEMMJM).

### The library is not honoring an area of the CSS/HTML standard.

For example, it doesn't render tag YYY or replicate the behavior of attribute XXX. This library is not meant for an exact compliance with the standard. First and foremost, because React Native imposes some constraints that we cannot overcome, and secondly, because the philosophy of the library is to let you customize rendering to fit your needs rather than strictly honoring the standards. Finally, because the [`react-native-webview`](https://github.com/react-native-community/react-native-webview) library fits this purpose.

However, we are always open to feature requests and propositions for enhancement regarding better compliance with the standards. You're more than welcomed to open a ticket (see Contributing > Opening Tickets) and discuss the feature on [our #general Discord channel](https://discord.gg/dbEMMJM).

### The library is not behaving as it claims or should.

For example:

A. The documentation says something, but the behavior differs.
B. The library should obviously have the behavior I'm expecting, but it doesn't.

**Recommendations**

1. Make sure your HTML snippet is compliant with the HTML5 spec.
   - A. Go to [https://validator.w3.org/nu/](https://validator.w3.org/nu/).
   - B. Select "Check by text input"
   - C. Paste your snippet in the body of the document.
   - D. Press "Check"
2. Make sure your issue isn't covered [by the docs](https://native-html.github.io/render/docs/intro).
3. Read the [FAQ](https://native-html.github.io/render/docs/faq).
4. Take a look at [native-html-render on StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/native-html-render) or [react-native-render-html on StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/react-native-render-html) for similar questions.
5. Take a look at [our issue tracker](https://github.com/native-html/render/issues) for similar questions.
6. If you still don't have a solution, you can choose one or more:
   - A. Submitting a Bug Report (see Contributing > Opening Tickets).
   - B. Going to [our Discord #support channel](https://discord.gg/dbEMMJM). Please note that if your issue is not trivial, we will probably ask you to fill a bug report anyway.

### I want to do X with this library, is it possible?

**Recommendations**

1. Make sure the feature isn't covered [by the docs](https://native-html.github.io/render/docs/intro).
2. Read the [FAQ](https://native-html.github.io/render/docs/faq).
3. Take a look at [native-html-render on StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/native-html-render) or [react-native-render-html on StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/react-native-render-html) for similar questions.
4. Take a look at [our issue tracker](https://github.com/native-html/render/issues) for similar questions.
5. If you still don't have an answer, you can choose one or more:
   - A. [Opening a StackOverflow post](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/ask) with the `@native-html/render` tag.
   - B. Submitting a Feature Request (see Contributing > Proposing a Feature or Enhancement).
   - C. Going to [our Discord #support channel](https://discord.gg/dbEMMJM).

### I am having trouble to understand how to use a specific feature of this library.

**Recommendations**

1. Carefully [read the docs](https://native-html.github.io/render/docs/intro).
2. Read the [FAQ](https://native-html.github.io/render/docs/faq).
3. If you still find difficult to use this feature, then we are lacking good documentation, and we should fix it. Go to [our Discord #support channel](https://discord.gg/dbEMMJM) and we will help you out.

## Contributing

### A Contributors' Guide

> Note: If you're starting to read this guide, well thanks for willing to contribute to this project! Your effort will be very much appreciated. **If you need help**, take a look at our dedicated document (see Getting Help).

### Opening Tickets

After you've read the relevant sections of this document, you can open a ticket through GitHub here: [https://github.com/native-html/render/issues/new/choose](https://github.com/native-html/render/issues/new/choose). Make sure you follow the appropriate template.

> Note: The art of filling good reports is as important and valued as the art of producing readable, maintainable code. Developers tend to rush when filling reports because their initiative stems from a place of frustration. This is very well understandable, but ineffective regarding the goal of solving one's problem. Consider the _time investment / benefits_ ratio: by filling a detailed bug report, you might have committed a chunk of your valuable time. But **your chances of having a fix merged rapidly have considerably increased**.

> Warning: By not following our guidelines and templates, you risk having your ticket closed without notice. Sorry about that... our time is also valuable, and we cannot help you if you don't help us in the process!

#### Submitting a Bug

> Caution: If you would like to report a problem, take a look around and see if someone already opened an issue about it (see the Getting Help section). If you are certain this is a new, unreported bug, you can submit a bug report [by opening a new issue](https://github.com/native-html/render/issues/new/choose).

The most important quality of your bug report is **reproducibility**. It means we can easily reproduce and investigate the bug to fix it as quickly as possible. If you've never heard of a "minimal reproducible example", take a look at this guide: [https://stackoverflow.com/help/mcve](https://stackoverflow.com/help/mcve). Bellow is a table of different types of reproductions:

> Tip: If you add screencasts, screenshots, debugging information, or any insights that can help us identify the failure as quickly as possible, you can consider each a bonus.

| Reproduction | Efficiency | Information |
|---|---|---|
| Regression Test | Highest | Offering a PR with a Test which reproduces the issue is the most efficient way to have your bug fixed rapidly. More details on the **dedicated section** (see Bug Reproduction). You are still required to open a bug report ticket, but you will be able to skip many steps. |
| Snack | High | A **Snack** is very convenient for you and for us. You can [**start from our template**](https://snack.expo.io/@jsamr/rnrhtml-template). **Make sure you set the appropriate version of this library.** |
| Git | High | A Git reproduction is as efficient as a Snack, albeit it might be a little extra work for you. |
| Code Snippet | Low | A snippet is better than nothing, but we don't consider it _high quality_ and might take more time to investigate. Please consider put your snippet into a **Snack**. It will take you 2 minutes to configure. |

Second important thing: try-out the latest version, including pre-releases! For more information on this topic, read the [Versions section of the README](https://github.com/native-html/render#versions). If you can try `master` branch, that would be even better, but we don't require it because it could contain breaking changes. To do so, simply run the following command:

```bash
npm install "github:native-html/render#master"
```

#### Proposing a Feature or Enhancement

* Feature requests and enhancements **must** be submitted [in our Canny feature tracker](https://native-html.canny.io/features).
* You can, **in addition**, consider writing an RFC (see Request For Comments) and offering it as a PR.

> Tip: You or your company need a feature? Consider [sponsorship or consultancy](https://github.com/sponsors/jsamr) and it will be delivered ASAP.

### Pull Requests

> Note: We require some criterion to accept a pull request. But don't worry, we're also willing to help. You're encouraged to start a [Github draft](https://github.blog/2019-02-14-introducing-draft-pull-requests/) and we will be glad to help you build it and make it comply with our requirements. If you have any question or need advise regarding your contribution, you can also ping us in our [Discord #contributing channel](https://discord.gg/MwrZmBb).

#### Bug Fixes

If your PR fixes a bug, you are required to implement a regression test to prove your fix is effective, but **don't worry, we will help you**. The simplest way is to look at [our test folder](https://github.com/native-html/render/tree/master/packages/render-html/src/__tests__) and copy/paste an existing _regression test_ to get inspiration. You are also advised to read our developing guide (see Development). If you know what the test should do, but don't know how to implement the test, you can add a "Testing Plan" section in the body of your PR.

#### Bug Reproduction

When you submit a bug ticket, the fastest path for us to resolve the issue is by providing a bug reproduction. Take a glance at [our test folder](https://github.com/native-html/render/tree/master/packages/render-html/src/__tests__) and get inspiration by looking at _regression tests_. You are also advised to read our developing guide (see Development). The PR is ready _when the test fails_.

#### Features

> Note: We recommend you use the [draft Github option](https://github.blog/2019-02-14-introducing-draft-pull-requests/) when you start a Feature PR!

If your PR provides new features, it means that the API of this library will likely change. You will be required to test the new feature. Take a look at [our test folder](https://github.com/native-html/render/tree/master/packages/render-html/src/__tests__). You are also advised to read our developing guide (see Development). If you're lost, we will be glad to help you, either on discord or within the PR on GitHub.

#### Request For Comments

> Note: RFC are propositions for new methods, behaviors and other API capabilities, or the exploration of an algorithmic challenge that is specific to this library. These are not Internet Society's RFCs! We don't have a rich multi-stage process. An RFC is either a draft, in discussion, or adopted (merged). We thereafter use versioning to polish and enhance those specifications.

RFC purpose is to offer drafts for new ideas which goes relatively in depth regarding the issues, consequences and caveats of a peculiar feature. We don't have strict requirements, but the structure should loosely resemble the following:

1. Problem Frame (what is the context and which issues this enhancement or feature will address).
2. Requirements (what are the behaviors required for this feature to be supported?).

You can take a look at drafts in [the `rfc` folder](https://github.com/native-html/render/tree/master/rfc) for inspiration.

> Note: We require RFCs to be written in **AsciiDoc**. If you know markdown, it is very easy to pick and it ends-up much more powerful and versatile. Their documentation is of excellent quality, as proven by their [writer's guide](https://asciidoctor.org/docs/asciidoc-writers-guide/).

#### Other

For other type of contributions (documentation, enhancements), we don't _a priori_ require anything particular.

## Development

### Participating in RNRH development

### Initializing the project

Clone the project:

```
git clone git@github.com:native-html/render.git
```

Then yarn-install:

```
cd @native-html/render
yarn install
```

### Package sources

Package sources are located in `packages/render-html`.

### Scripts

The project is using Yarn Berry's workspaces. There is an alias to work from `@native-html/render` workspace:

```
yarn render
```

You can then run the following commands:

| Most significant scripts | Description |
|---|---|
| `yarn render-html test:jest --watch` | Launch jest test in watch mode |
| `yarn render-html test:ts` | Run Typescript typechecking |
| `yarn render-html test:lint` | Run linter |
| `yarn render-html build` | Transpile TS to ES |

### Demo app

```
yarn build:tools
yarn render-html build
```

From now-on, you should be able to try out the demo app with

```
yarn demo start
```

### Documentation

All the doc pages are React components available in `doc-tools/doc-pages/src/pages` and are built for both the Discovery expo app and website.

## Maintaining and Releasing

### A Maintainers' Guide

### Semantic Versioning

We _must_ follow Semantic Versioning rules when publishing packages, and especially:

- Never publish breaking changes, including regarding tooling and installation, between two versions of the same MAJOR.
- Keep the semantics right between MINOR and PATCHES. MINORs convey new features while patches convey fixes.

If you have a doubt, read the Semantic Versioning standard, v2.0 at [https://semver.org](https://semver.org). It's not that long.

### Branching

#### Development branches

The branching system is highly coupled with Semantic Versioning. We support backporting fixes to different MAJOR versions. To do so, we adopt the following conventions:

- `master` is the ultimate development branch for the upmost MAJOR, accepting PRs, fixes, new features... etc.
- Any development branch for a MAJOR strictly inferior to master's MAJOR will have a name composed with the following pattern:

```
dev/MAJOR.x
```

These development branches will be used to cherry-pick backports from `master`.

#### Release branches

> Note: Release branches target a MAJOR.MINOR release. Patches within this minor will get merged. This is especially useful to hold references to documentation for a specific release while accounting for the fact it can be a moving target.

Release branches have a name composed with the following pattern:

```
release/MAJOR.MINOR
```

#### Transient branches

> Warning: Transient branches should never be worked on by more than one person at a time, unless authors are completely aware of their collaboration.

> Note: Transient branches should be based on master and rebased before merging to `master`. They should be deleted after merged to master.

These branches are meant for short-term development cycles such as pull requests. These branches' names should follow the following pattern:

```
PREFIX/QUALIFIER
```

| PREFIX | Description | QUALIFIER | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| `feat` | New features | The issue number this feat will cover, or a slug summarizing the feature | `feat/001` `feat/inline-css` |
| `fix` | Bug fixes | The issue number this fix will address, or a slug summarizing this fix. | `fix/001` `fix/start-attribute` |
| `reg` | (Anti) regression tests | The issue number this test will reproduce. | `reg/001` |
| `tests` | Coverage or other tests | A slug summarizing the areas covered by the test(s). | `tests/image-renderer` |
| `rfc` | Requests For Comments | A slug summarizing the area covered by the RFC. | `rfc/whitespaces` |
| `opt` | Optimizations | The issue number this optimization will address, or a slug summarizing the optimization. | `opt/103` `opt/rendering-cycles` |

### Publishing

> Caution: Pre-releases should be prepared from `master` or `dev/MINOR.x` (see Branching).

The publishing cycle entails pre-releases, which are usually tagged on npm with `next`. The table below describes the relationship between releases names, npm tags and their semantics. Custom npm tags can also be used to denote a new MAJOR version in early-stage development.

| Release type | Npm tag | Version suffix | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unstable | `unstable` | `-alpha.x` | Features and API can evolve. |
| Frozen | `next` | `-beta.x` | Features are frozen. Eventually, new fixes and optimizations can be merged. |
| Stable | `latest` `release/MAJOR.MINOR` | _none_ | Stable releases. |

#### Pre-releases

##### Prerequisites

- [ ] Tests are passing;
- [ ] I'm on the `master` (or a `dev/MINOR.x` branch if I'm backporting fixes);
- [ ] If the release is frozen, I've updated the changelog with a `next` entry;
- [ ] I have changed the version in  `package.json`;
- [ ] I have commited my changes;
- [ ] I have tagged this very commit with `v<semver>`, replacing `<semver>` with the version in `package.json`.

##### Steps

We use [release-it](https://github.com/release-it/release-it) utility to release new versions. You will need to provide a GIHUB_TOKEN environment variable to publish the release on Github.

1. Run

   ```
   yarn render-html release-it --preRelease=beta --npm.tag=next 
   ```

   for a beta or

   ```
   yarn render-html release-it --preRelease=alpha --npm.tag=unstable
   ```

   for an alpha release. Eventually, edit manually the CHANGELOG.md file to add extra information.
2. If this is the first pre-release, create a new issue on Github to be pinned, asking for feedback for this pre-release. This issue must have the `release` label.
3. Release the new documentation website with

   ```
   yarn publish:website
   ```

   You will need to pass a USER environment variable to this command if your github user has a different name than your logged system user.
4. Release the new discovery app with

   ```
   yarn publish:discovery
   ```

#### Releases

##### Prerequisites

- [ ] Tests are passing;
- [ ] I'm on the `master` (or a `dev/MINOR.x` branch if I'm backporting fixes);
- [ ] I've updated the changelog with a `<version>` entry;
- [ ] I have changed the version in `package.json`;
- [ ] I have commited my changes;
- [ ] I have tagged this very commit with `v<semver>`, replacing `<semver>` with the version in `package.json`.

##### Steps

We use [release-it](https://github.com/release-it/release-it) utility to release new versions. You will need to provide a GIHUB_TOKEN environment variable to publish the release on Github.

1. Run

   ```
   yarn render-html release-it
   ```

   Eventually, edit manually the CHANGELOG.md file to add extra information.
2. Release the new documentation website with

   ```
   yarn publish:website
   ```

   You will need to pass a USER environment variable to this command if your github user has a different name than your logged system user.
3. Release the new discovery app with

   ```
   yarn publish:discovery
   ```

**If this publication was a backport (from a `dev/MINOR.x` branch), you must cherry-pick the version commit into master.**

A. Checkout and pull master

```
git switch master
git pull
```

B. Cherry-pick the commit you have previously made on `dev/MINOR.x` branch.

```
git cherry-pick <commit-id>
```

If you must resolve conflicts, make sure:

- [ ] The new changelog entry is positioned in the appropriate order;
- [ ] The `package.json` version remains the upmost.

## Documentation Tooling

Documentation primitives for both mobile app and website.
